title: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island
description: Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram
body: Presenter Maya Jama has announced she is stepping down as the host of reality TV show Love Island after three years.The 32-year-old wrote on Instagram alongside a highlights reel of her on the programme that it was "time to throw myself into something new"."While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I'll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever," the TV and radio presenter said.Jama's announcement comes hot on the heels of an appearance as a contestant on Celebrity Traitors that won her praise and speculation in the Times, external that she could "get £1m per deal" thanks to her success.Thanking fans and the production team on Love Island, she said she had an "unforgettable time" on the programme."I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the nine incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I've loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show.But she added: "I've always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then."Jama landed her biggest presenting role to date as the host of the reality TV show in 2023, taking over from Laura Whitmore.The programme couples contestants together who then complete a range of tasks and keep swapping in the hope of meeting the love of their life.An ITV spokesperson said: "Maya has been a fantastic and much loved host on Love Island - we thank her for everything she has brought to the show over the last three years and wish her every continued success."Love Island is one of the most popular reality TV shows in the UK but the series has polarised viewers, with some arguing the show is misogynistic and raising concerns about the welfare of contestants.Ofcom has previously received tens of thousands of complaints about Love Island including about alleged misogynistic and bullying behaviour by some contestants.The watchdog has previously described the show as "emotionally charged" with "confrontational scenes" that can upset some viewers.Jama first built her profile through radio including a role on Rinse FM, before landing a presenting role on BBC Radio 1 in 2018.She went on to present a string of television programmes, including Channel 4's Stand Up To Cancer and ITV2's Don't Hate the Playaz, before taking over as host of BBC Three's Glow Up: Britain's Next Make-Up Star in 2021.The presenter was recently watched by millions in the Celebrity Traitors final, and competed as a traitor alongside actor Richard E Grant, Youtuber King Kenny and comedian James Acaster during the series.One commentator at the time said that, despite not winning the show, she had emerged as a winner of sorts as she was able to portray herself as "less like the presenter of Love Island and more like a genuinely versatile television star".Her Celebrity Traitors appearance came after she made her acting debut in the second series of Guy Ritchie's Netflix drama The Gentlemen alongside Theo James and Kaya Scodelario.Jama had auditioned for the cult Channel 4 series Skins, set in her hometown of Bristol, when she was 15, reaching the final stage for a role in the show that launched the careers of actors Daniel Kaluuya and Dev Patel.She moved to London when she was 16 to pursue a career in the entertainment industry.She began presenting a weekly music video countdown for production company JumpOff TV before joining MTV in 2014 as a presenter on The Wrap Up.Jama became the youngest person to host the MOBO Awards, alongside Marvin Humes, in 2017.

schema.headline: Maya Jama steps down as host of reality TV show Love Island

title: Canary Islands: 34 dead after migrant boat sinks off Senegal en route to Europe
description: At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an offici
body: At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency (APS) reports, citing an official source.The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, but the number of people still missing was yet to be established.The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands.Spanish migrant rights group Walking Borders recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canary Islands between January and May 2026, the highest toll among the routes it monitors.Saliou Diouf, founder of Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of other people on board was yet to be established, as search operations continued.President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has expressed his condolences to the victims' families and urged Senegalese nationals not risk their lives on the dangerous sea crossings.In a statement posted on X, he pledged to intensify efforts to dismantle the networks organising the journeys."We will relentlessly continue the fight against those who organise these crossings and the work that gives our young people reasons to hope here," he said.The tragedy comes amid renewed concerns over the dangers facing migrant attempting to reach Europe by sea.Walking Borders estimates that about 21 people died for every 100 who reached the Canary Islands during the period it monitored.Senegalese authorities said they had intercepted another boat, on Friday, carrying 142 migrants attempting to reach Spain.Those on board included 23 women, two babies and two other children. Police said the group comprised nationals of Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea and Nigeria.Meanwhile, a state of emergency was declared on the Spanish island of El Hierro on Saturday following a surge in migrant arrivals.More than 3,300 people have reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of November, according to local authorities.This amounts to almost a third of the population on the island, one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants arriving from West Africa. Fernando Clavijo, president of the Canary Islands regional government, described the situation as "absolutely unsustainable," reports the Reuters news agency.The route has grown in prominence amid tighter controls and increased cooperation between European countries and North African states, which may have diverted some journeys away from the central Mediterranean.Limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks are among the factors driving people to leave Senegal, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM).For many young people, the prospect of finding work and earning more abroad remains a powerful incentive, despite the risks of crossing the Atlantic in overcrowded boat.Nearly one in four young people in Senegal was unemployed in the second quarter of 2026, according to the country's statistics agency. The figure highlights the challenge facing President Faye's government as it seeks to create jobs for a predominantly young population that overwhelmingly voted for him in the 2024 elections.In a statement on Sunday, Senegal's interior ministry said it would continue efforts to combat people-smuggling networks, including by strengthening cooperation with neighbouring countries.

schema.headline: Canary Islands: 34 dead after migrant boat sinks off Senegal en route to Europe

title: Liverpool: Alisson Becker wants to sign new contract
description: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker wants to stay at the club beyond the end of the season, when his current contract expires.The 34-year-old joined f
body: Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker wants to stay at the club beyond the end of the season, when his current contract expires.The 34-year-old joined from Roma for £66.8m in 2018 and has made 347 appearances for the Reds."Yes [I want to stay], in my mind. I'm focused on playing every game but in my mind I'm happy to stay," said Alisson."That depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay - I'm happy here and my family is happy here. "I'm still hungry for titles and to delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can, so that's my thinking."Last week, Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola said he did not know if this would be Alisson's last season at the club but hoped the goalkeeper could "continue for more time".Asked if he has had conversations over a new deal, Alisson said: "No, but my agent is talking with the club."The Brazil keeper did consider a move to Juventus earlier this year but ultimately chose to stay at Anfield.After a difficult week - with Liverpool losing to Arsenal and then Fenerbahce - Alisson made a number of crucial saves in Sunday's win at Crystal Palace.The goalkeeper says Liverpool now need to find consistency in order to challenge for silverware."Our reality is that we're not doing as well as we can. It doesn't mean that we are not doing well - we are doing well in so many games - but the consistency is not there yet," he said."We have a top manager, top players. We are capable of great things but as a team we need to get to a point where we feel: 'We are OK now. We have the confidence. We have everything that's needed to win.' "We are building that. I hope we get there really quick but it takes time. "We have to be patient but as players, in our mind, we don't have time to waste."This is the first time Alisson has discussed his contract situation this season and, judging by the way he spoke after a superb performance at Selhurst Park, there is a clear desire on his part to stay at Liverpool.Giorgi Mamardashvili, 26, is waiting in the wings, while highly rated 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans will move to Liverpool from Genk in the summer, so Iraola's side will not be short of goalkeeping options - but it would be a huge call if they do allow Alisson to leave on a free transfer.His distribution has not been up to the standard we are used to in recent weeks, and that was ruthlessly punished against Arsenal, but the string of saves he made against Palace were a timely reminder that he is still a world-class goalkeeper. This season, Liverpool have kept four clean sheets in 10 Premier League games but have conceded 10 goals in four Champions League matches, with Alisson playing every minute in both competitions so far. He is still a leader within the side and was named as one of Iraola's vice-captains at the start of the season.Alisson did assess his options last season but with senior figures like Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson leaving, he opted to proceed with a one-year extension.With Virgil van Dijk's contract also set to expire at the end of the season, sporting director Julian Ward has two very important decisions to make when it comes to the future of two men who have been a constant for Liverpool since 2018. Of course, both command hefty wages, but this is a young Liverpool side trying to find their way under Iraola - and the head coach will be aware of the importance of two experienced players who have been with the club for such a long time.Perhaps a one-year extension can be offered to Alisson which could allow Brughmans to learn from the Brazilian but, at 34, he may be looking for the security of something longer term.Either way, Liverpool's hierarchy will have a keen eye on how Alisson fares as the season progresses. If he can carry on performing like he did against Palace, then a new contract will be a no-brainer.

schema.headline: Liverpool: Alisson Becker wants to sign new contract

title: Nations Championship: Matt Dawson column - England make massive step up in 45-22 win vs Australia
description: In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on an impressive 45-22 win for Steve Borthwick's side against Australia
body: In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on an impressive 45-22 win for Steve Borthwick's side against Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday.Beating Australia with their record points tally against the Wallabies was a very positive way for England to start the autumn series, given the break they have had and how the beginning of the year went.England were very accurate, very disciplined, creative and genuinely did not give Australia a sniff.Before the game, I was expecting Australia to provide much more of a stern test. Some people might be a bit too critical of Australia, saying they did not turn up, but I think it edges more towards how well England played than how average Australia were.I am not saying by any stretch that it was the perfect performance but, all in all, it was a massive step up from the Six Nations and even from the Nations Championship games in the summer.Intensity, accuracy and discipline in abundanceFigure caption, Watch: England score seven tries in record-breaking win against AustraliaA couple of days before the Australia game, Jamie George said the England team had been galvanised by a newspaper article which claimed the end of their summer tour had been marked by player unrest over head coach Borthwick's leadership.When you are inside those international camps, you are very deliberate in staying tight and not letting anybody in in whatever way, shape or form, therefore you become very sensitive to any kind of criticism.There is a reason for doing that - it draws you together and allows you to create a bit more determination and drive to be successful.You could see England's intensity, their accuracy and their discipline. All the things that have maybe been highlighted over the past nine months as things England have been lacking, there was an abundance of all of it.As much as it is easy to try to pick holes in England because it is England, sometimes you have got to pat people on the back and say they got it right.The opposition was dangerous with good individual players, but from the off England's tactics were spot on. Their decision-making was controlled and they looked like a very well-drilled side.How England might unlock the best of SladeEngland's back three of George Furbank, Tommy Freeman and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso caused plenty of problems for Australia, but I think you have to include Fin Smith and Henry Slade in that as well.Potentially, there is something in that backline that may allow us to see the Slade we see for Exeter that we have not seen as much for England.Having the likes of Feyi-Waboso, Freeman and Furbank around Slade and them understanding the sorts of positions he can get them into - there might be some long-term benefits to that.Feyi-Waboso is X-factor, there is no question about that. For his early disallowed try, he shifted his weight and beat someone with that pace - I do not think there are many people in the world who could do that.When you have got players like him who can do that regularly, all of a sudden you are getting momentum.There was a massive difference in ruck speed and in momentum; England were getting lined up defensively and pushing Australia back, whereas when you have got players like Feyi-Waboso and Ben Earl, and then when Henry Pollock comes on as well, you have got plenty of players who can break the line in traffic and it makes attacking that much easier.Fin Smith is leading the team, he looks like he is a general and in control of the game.He has got a safe pair of hands and communication from Seb Atkinson, he has got vision from Slade and then a back three that if you give them half a chance, they are going to bust the line, create opportunities and probably finish.There were bits of Sunday's game where if New Zealand were doing it, everybody would be ranting and raving about how complete some of those tries were.Pollock's flexibility a fantastic weaponImage source, Press AssociationImage caption, Henry Pollock has five tries in four Nations Championship matches, with only New Zealand's Will Jordan (six) scoring moreFeyi-Waboso's injury meant Pollock came off the bench to play in an unfamiliar position on the wing and he ended up scoring two of England's seven tries.He did very well considering he was on for a whole half. Going forward, what is the difference having Pollock there? He has got a winger's speed, the step, great hands, the power and the bulk that other wingers do not have and he is going to be a handful for the opposition.Defensively, he was tested a couple of times and that is inevitable, but to have that flexibility on the bench allows England to have that six-two split because you have got a player who can now pretty much cover so many positions.As great as it was, and I am sure he absolutely loved it, unfortunately he is probably inking himself in to be quite a significant bench player moving forward, which is not really what I think he would like to be labelled as.Selfishly, from an England point of view, it is a fantastic weapon to have.The whole bench did really well and made a difference. It goes all the way back to selection, something Borthwick has previously come under fire for a little bit.It does not mean that just because he has got one right, the autumn is going to go swimmingly well, but from the off the selection has been right, the gameplan was a bit more expansive than I thought it was going to be and they absolutely nailed the execution.Will England back it up against Japan?Tactically, I loved the balance of the England performance; a really dominant set-piece, driving mauls and in-your-face defence.England have maybe always been like that but have lacked the discipline to go with it.Against Australia, they proved they have the capability to be disciplined and maintain concentration - and I want to see that over the next three weeks.Can they, under more pressure - because they are going to face more pressure, particularly against New Zealand - still maintain that discipline and decision-making?They have got the assets to overpower Japan, but can they do it by giving away fewer than 10 penalties? Can they do it by having 15 people on the pitch for 80 minutes?All of the little things they have been after, can they do them against a team they should beat comfortably?If they can, then when they go into the New Zealand game with it all to play for and when they are really testing themselves, they are going to have huge momentum.Matt Dawson was speaking to BBC Sport's Phil Cartwright.

schema.headline: Nations Championship: Matt Dawson column - England make massive step up in 45-22 win vs Australia

title: NFL results: Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos grind out wins in week nine
description: Packers & Bengals win in style - NFL week nineFigure caption, 'Spectacular' catches and toe-tapping skills - NFL best playsByBen CollinsBBC Sport jour
body: Packers & Bengals win in style - NFL week nineFigure caption, 'Spectacular' catches and toe-tapping skills - NFL best playsByBen CollinsBBC Sport journalistThe potential Super Bowl contenders are starting to emerge in the NFL with the regular season having reached its halfway point this weekend.The San Francisco 49ers have the league's best record after winning on Sunday and will be joined on 7-1 by either the Buffalo Bills or Minnesota Vikings - provided they do not have a tie in Monday's game.The Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos both ground out hard-fought wins to improve to 7-2 heading into their bye weeks.The Cincinnati Bengals put on a show as the NFL's international series continued while the Green Bay Packers outclassed one of last season's Super Bowl teams.Here are the top stories from week nine in the NFL.Broncos claim NFL recordAfter winning at defending champions Seattle last week, Chicago looked set for another impressive victory as they charged into a 14-0 lead against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Sunday's primetime game.Bears quarterback Caleb Williams then threw a career-high four interceptions before the Bucs drew level with three minutes remaining.But Williams managed to lead the hosts into field-goal range, with Cairo Santos making a 38-yard kick as time expired to beat the Bucs 27-24 for Chicago's fourth straight win.The Bears are now second in the NFC North, the only division in which all four teams have a winning record, but will go top if the Vikings lose to the Bills on Monday.Denver are top of the AFC West after they scored two touchdowns in the final quarter and sacked Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young with just over a minute left to clinch a 26-21 road win.Not only did it extend the Broncos' winning run to five but was their 16th straight win in one-score games in the regular season - a new NFL record.Bengals put on a show in SpainImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Touchdown scorers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins entertained the Spanish crowd with a matador and bull celebrationJoe Burrow attended Milan fashion week this summer and modelled in Paris in 2024, but this week he visited Madrid to play his first international game.The Cincinnati Bengals quarterback vowed to put on a show at the Bernabeu Stadium in the seventh of a record nine international games this season, and the Bengals did just that as they beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 to go 6-2.After being involved in six touchdowns last week, Burrow played a part in another four in Spain. The 29-year-old completed 24 of his 29 passes for 271 yards to cement himself as a contender for his first Most Valuable Player award.Ja'Marr Chase had a season-high 155 receiving yards as the Bengals scored more than 30 points for a fourth straight game – tying a team record.The Bengals are now 6-2 and joint-top of the AFC North with the Pittsburgh Steelers, who they face in next Sunday's primetime game.Their divisional rivals the Cleveland Browns lost 23-22 at the New Orleans Saints in overtime.Packers ruin return of Patriots legendsImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Rob Gronkowski won three Super Bowls with New England and one with Tampa Bay, all with Tom Brady at quarterbackFour-time Super Bowl winner Rob Gronkowski was inducted into the New England Patriots' hall of fame while his former team-mate Tom Brady returned to Gillette Stadium for the first time in his broadcasting career.Yet they had to watch Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love put on a masterclass as the Packers romped to a 45-27 win against a New England team that reached last season's Super Bowl. It was the most points the Patriots had allowed at home since 1970.Love went deep time and again, racking up 372 passing yards, three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. Wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden became the first Green Bay players to each claim more than 150 receiving yards and a touchdown in the same game since 1942.Brady and Gronkowski are third all-time for passing yards from a quarterback-tight end duo (9,186) and Kansas City Chiefs pair Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce went top of that list on Sunday.Mahomes brushed off an injury scare against the New York Jets to ensure he and Kelce surpassed Philip Rivers and Antonio Gates (9,352) to reach 9,360 during a 35-12 win for the Chiefs.Garrett stars on Rams returnImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Aaron Donald (99) or Myles Garrett (95) have won the NFL's defensive player of the year award in five of the past nine yearsMyles Garrett and Aaron Donald finally played together for the first time as the Los Angeles Rams won 20-13 at the Washington Commanders.After making his Rams debut in Australia in week one, Garrett needed knee surgery and Donald didn't make his return from retirement until week two.While Donald, 35, is still waiting for his first sack of the season, Garrett claimed three and forced a fumble to help the former Super Bowl favourites clinch a third straight win.Puka Nacua racked up 150 receiving yards and a touchdown but could join fellow wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) on the sidelines as he injured a knee. Nacua will have an MRI on Monday.Although the Rams are now 5-4, their NFC West rivals the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks both got back to winning ways.The 49ers (7-1) won 38-17 against the Las Vegas Raiders while defending champions Seattle (5-4) beat the Arizona Cardinals 17-3.More Colts trades before deadline?The Indianapolis Colts have already begun a rebuild, trading away two key players during the season, and they could have more big-name departures before the trade deadline on Tuesday.The Colts slipped to 2-7 with a 27-23 loss to the Dallas Cowboys but had already been in talks over running back Jonathan Taylor, their prized asset.They have reportedly taken calls about quarterback Daniel Jones too, while wide receiver Josh Downs has requested a trade.The New York Giants withdrew an offer for Taylor but head coach John Harbaugh said that "things do change" after Sunday's 19-11 win over the Philadelphia Eagles – a seventh straight loss for Philly and the Giants' first win at their divisional rivals in 13 years.Down to their third-choice quarterback, the Baltimore Ravens have completed a trade for Jacoby Brissett from Arizona but despite speculation over Derrick Henry, the Ravens reportedly have no intention of trading the veteran running back.Arizona pair Budda Baker and Josh Sweat have been linked with a trade while there has been interest in wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr, who has slipped down the pecking order at the 6-2 Jacksonville Jaguars.

schema.headline: NFL results: Chicago Bears and Denver Broncos grind out wins in week nine

title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says
description: Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquir
body: Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.The inquiry's first report, published this summer, concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done"."This isn't just the responsibility of schools but calls for action from across society," she said.The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, external was commissioned by the multi-academy trust Star Academies, and is supported by the Department for Education.It spoke to thousands of young people and their parents, as well as hundreds of teachers.Education data about white working class pupils was also analysed as part of the year-long review, looking at the 1.25 million young people in England who are white British and in receipt of free school meals.The inquiry found a growing belief among white working-class families that the current education system does not guarantee future success.In the summer, the inquiry also acknowledged that the true scale of white working-class disadvantage is "likely to be substantially larger", as the education data they looked at did not include families who were on low incomes but did not receive free school meals.Since then, all families receiving Universal Credit have become eligible for free school meals.Under the new phase of the inquiry, practical recommendations for government, schools, colleges and other organisations working with white working-class communities will be developed.This action will include a research programme looking at the routes taken by teenagers aged 14 to 19, investigating how schools can work with communities to provide clearer pathways into further study and successful employment.The new phase of the inquiry will also look at how schools can ensure the transition from primary to secondary school builds strong foundations."Right now, too many white working-class children are falling behind at every stage of their education," Powell said."That is why I am backing this independent inquiry to get to the heart of the barriers holding children back - from their first steps into school, through to the opportunities and choices they have as teenagers into further study, training or work."It comes after Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced plans to open up new technical routes from age 14 in England over the summer.The prime minister said he was "on a mission" to reduce the number of young people not in education, employment or training - known as "Neet".Currently, nearly a million young people are classed as Neet. Former minister Alan Milburn's interim report, external found that children who are not school-ready at aged four or five are nearly three times as likely to be Neet by ages 16 to 17.A final report by Milburn is expected to set out his recommendations for tackling the issue in the coming weeks.

schema.headline: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

title: Woman says Fayed's brother drugged and sexually abused her at Highland estate
description: Figure caption, Al Fayed's brother 'assaulted me at Scottish estate'BySuzanne AllanBBC ScotlandUpdated 2 hours agoA woman has told BBC Scotland how sh
body: Figure caption, Al Fayed's brother 'assaulted me at Scottish estate'BySuzanne AllanBBC ScotlandUpdated 2 hours agoA woman has told BBC Scotland how she was trafficked to the Highlands, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner by Salah Fayed, the brother of former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed.Jill, whose name has been changed for legal reasons, said she was a young Harrods employee when she was recruited to what she believed was an executive training scheme in the 1990s.Speaking for the first time about the abuse that took place in Scotland, Jill said she was flown on the Fayed family's private jet to Balnagown, their estate in Easter Ross, where she was repeatedly assaulted.She is one of hundreds of women who have alleged abuse by the Fayed brothers.Since Mohamed Al Fayed's death in 2023, hundreds of women and girls have alleged they were sexually abused by him.His brother Salah, who died of pancreatic cancer in 2010, has also been accused of abuse by numerous women.Image caption, Mohamed Al Fayed owned Balnagown Estate in the HighlandsPolice Scotland said three people had been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims at Balnagown and inquiries remained ongoing.Speaking to BBC Scotland, Jill described Salah Fayed as "a very cruel man" who exploited her vulnerabilities and exercised near-total control over her life.She said she began her career at Harrods working for Mohamed Al Fayed in a heavily-monitored office staffed largely by young women, where access was tightly controlled and employees were discouraged from interacting with others.Soon afterwards, she was assigned to work for Salah Fayed."I thought it might be better," she said. "Mohamed seemed creepy to me."Instead, she said, her situation deteriorated rapidly."I was taken to Scotland twice. Both times it was on their private jet."When you flew there, you flew into Inverness and their vehicles would pick you up from the airport and take you to the estate."Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Salah Fayed with his brother Mohamed Al Fayed bought Harrods in 1985On the Balnagown Estate there were three residences, one for each brother.  Jill describes Salah Fayed's house as smaller than Mohamed Al Fayed's, overlooking the valley with the forest behind and isolated.She alleged that by this stage Salah Fayed had begun giving her illegal substances."The first time he forced me to take the drugs he tried to trick me into taking them," she said.  "He had me locked in a room. He said 'you need to take this, it's good for you'. He lied about what it was and when I refused he screamed at me and forced me to take it."The drugs were part of his method of assaulting me."Jill said he controlled what she ate, wore and who she spoke to.She said most of what happened was against her will."I was isolated, for most of the time," she said. "He was a very cruel man.  "He knew I had some vulnerabilities and he exploited them.  He made me feel I was a terrible person."Image source, PA MediaImage caption, Mohamed Al Fayed has been accused by dozens of womenJill said escaping the situation was difficult and that she only gradually came to understand the extent of what had happened to her."By the time I got away, I was very aware of what he was doing and it took some effort to get away," she said.  "I was by then aware that I could not have been the only one."I tried to raise the alarm, I tried to warn people."Salah Fayed was one of three Fayed brothers who purchased Harrods, the luxury Knightsbridge department store, in 1985.If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line.After his death, Mohamed Al Fayed was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary Predator at Harrods that aired in 2024. The BBC also published the podcast World of Secrets that same year.Since those allegations more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims."Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."Human trafficking The Metropolitan Police is separately investigating allegations linked to Mohamed Al Fayed and those suspected of facilitating his offending.It said it was one of the largest and most complex investigations it was currently undertaking."Seven suspects have so far been interviewed under caution on suspicion of offences including aiding and abetting rape and sexual assault, assisting the commission of sexual offences, and human trafficking for sexual exploitation," a Met Police statement said."To date, 168 victims have now come forward. We will continue to assess victim testimonies for evidence of human trafficking." In a confidential note, shared with survivors, of a meeting between the Met and the All Party Parliamentary Group (APPG) for Survivors of Fayed and Harrods, it said about 70 people had been referred to the Home Office as potential victims of trafficking.Jill told BBC Scotland she was aware of other women who alleged they were abused by Salah Fayed in Scotland, although some have never reported their experiences publicly.She said she agreed with calls from some of the victims for a statutory public inquiry.  And she said she was speaking out because of worries the police investigations were not looking far enough.Jill has contacted the Metropolitan Police and is also pursuing legal action.Harrods, which is no longer owned by the Fayed family, said it recognised the "remarkable bravery" of survivors who had come forward and supported them in their pursuit of justice.The retailer has previously established a redress scheme for survivors of abuse linked to Mohamed Al Fayed.Jill said any compensation would be a partial refund for the impact on her life. "You've lost years of your life," she said. "You've had all these treatment costs, it's impacted your career, impacted your family, so yes they do need to put that right.""The girl I was when I was sent to that man is gone," Jill said."I don't know who she would have been or what her life would have been like.  "My life's work has been recovering from this. It has been a bitter, bitter, decades-long struggle."'They were part of a wider network'Liberal Democrat MP Wendy Chamberlain, who co-chairs the APPG, said criminal justice outcomes were still possible.She told the BBC's Radio Scotland Breakfast programme: "Fayed and his brother did not act alone. "They were part of a wider network of enablers who brought women to them to be abused."And it's not just about Harrod's either."There are other locations. We've had testimony in relation to Fulham Football Club, where abuse was perpetrated."Chamberlain said the APPG was due to meet the Metropolitan Police again before Christmas and was working on a report for MPs.She added: "Beyond that we want to look at other aspects."We know, for example, that there were doctors involved in some medical examinations of victims of trafficking and so we want to look very closely at that."The BBC has contacted the Balnagown Estate for comment twice and as yet they have not replied.

schema.headline: Woman says Fayed's brother drugged and sexually abused her at Highland estate

title: James Bond: What we know so far about the next 007 film
description: The movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for Prisoners, Sicario, Arrival, Blade Runner 2049 and the recent Dune trilogy starring Timothée
body: The movie will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, known for Prisoners, Sicario, Arrival, Blade Runner 2049 and the recent Dune trilogy starring Timothée Chalamet."Some of my earliest movie-going memories are connected to 007," the French-Canadian director said last year. "I grew up watching James Bond films with my father, ever since Dr. No with Sean Connery. I'm a die-hard Bond fan. To me, he's sacred territory."He added: "I intend to honour the tradition and open the path for many new missions to come. This is a massive responsibility, but also, incredibly exciting for me and a huge honour."Bond 26 will be written by Steven Knight, known for TV series such as Peaky Blinders and House of Guinness, and films including Burnt, Spencer, Locke and The Girl in the Spider's Web.Knight has said it had always been on his "bucket list" to write a Bond film, adding that he felt he was "doing my duty for King and country" by joining the franchise. He told the BBC he planned to "write the character, not the actor", adding: "The thing with Bond is it's its own universe and franchise. So there are certain rules. "Obviously you have to move it along, but I love where it sits. I love that it's British. I love that it's not DC or Marvel... So I feel a responsibility to the text."With the change in ownership and a new creative team now in place, the new Bond film is likely to make a fresh start.It would be difficult to continue the story chronologically given the ending of 2021's No Time To Die, but that still leaves producers with plenty of options. A different version of James Bond, who exists in a different universe, would be easily pulled off in an era where audiences are used to major film franchises restarting in a different world or timeline.Bond 26 could even be set in a significantly earlier era - an idea that gained more popularity after Tony Gilroy revealed he and fellow director Steven Soderbergh previously pitched a 1960s version, external of Bond.Separately, actor Ralph Fiennes recently said, external he had once been in talks to play Bond, and had suggested producers make a "black and white and very sort of film noir-y" version set in the 1950s.Neither idea materialised, but the suggestion went down well with some Bond fans, who noted a period piece would help make the film truer to Ian Fleming's original character and books.Exactly what shape the next film takes will become clear at a later stage. For now, fans are hoping that Christmas could be about to come early this year, as the world awaits the imminent announcement of the next actor to play 007.

schema.headline: James Bond: What we know so far about the next 007 film

title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
description: The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by env
body: The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.The government has been consulting on reducing its 80% rule and a significant reduction is now expected.Downing Street has insisted no decision has been made.A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company. The key meetings on the subject will instead be chaired by Cabinet Office minister Louise Haigh.Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point."Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.Last month, it said, external reducing targets could damage "the investment certainty needed to deliver the infrastructure, innovation and services required for the transition to zero-emission transport".Asked if climate change was no longer a big priority, Health Minister Karin Smyth said the government was committed to its emissions targets."This country is doing great work in terms of our transition and looking at renewables – that's a key part of growth in different parts of the country," she told BBC Breakfast.She added that the prime minister would have "a good story to tell" when meeting other leaders at COP31.A government spokesperson said: "We are committed to the phase out of all new cars relying solely on petrol and diesel engines by 2030, and to 100% of new car and van sales being zero emission by 2035, and our legally binding net zero targets."The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders welcomed the government's review of the EV targets when it was announced in the summer. Last week, head of the association Mike Hawes said transitioning to electric vehicles had come at a "heavy cost" with billions spent on discounts to drive demand in electric vehicles.He said the government's targets could not be achieved "without putting at risk any future investment".Net zero means balancing the amount of planet-warming "greenhouse" gases produced by human activities with the amount being actively removed from the atmosphere.The government's policy to phase out petrol and diesel vehicle sales has undergone multiple changes since it was first introduced by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2020.His successor Rishi Sunak pushed back the timeline to 2035, and the Burnham government set up a review of the EV sales targets in August.Sunak introduced phased targets for EV sales in the UK, known as the Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEV) mandate.Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year. The target was 28% for 2025, 33% for 2026, and so on until it reaches 80% by 2030.Pressure in the European Union saw the bloc scrap a similar plan to ban new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035, particularly from countries with large auto industries such as Germany.The Conservative Party has also vowed to abandon the petrol car ban if it wins the next election, with leader Kemi Badenoch calling it a "well-meaning, but ultimately destructive piece of legislation".Green Party leader Zack Polanski said the government was "building up a shocking record of backsliding and bad decisions on climate issues".

schema.headline: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

title: Dormouse numbers may be helped by warmer summers - survey
description: But conservationists caution that many questions remain unanswered, and say protecting the woodlands and hedgerows where dormice live remains essentia
body: But conservationists caution that many questions remain unanswered, and say protecting the woodlands and hedgerows where dormice live remains essential to their long-term survival.The only native species of dormice in the UK is the hazel dormouse. Once widespread across the country, they are now largely confined to southern England and parts of Wales. They have become much rarer as large areas of woodland are lost and so far native populations have disappeared from around 20 English counties.The National Dormouse Monitoring Programme, led by the conservation charity People's Trust for Endangered Species (PTES),  has been monitoring sites in England and Wales since 1998. It found that since 2000, dormouse numbers have fallen by almost 60%, equivalent to an average annual decline of 3.5%. More recently, however, there are signs that trend may be reversing. The data suggests the population increased by almost 10% between 2020 and 2025, although researchers stress there is considerable uncertainty around that estimate.The apparent improvement coincides with a period of warmer, drier-than-average springs and summers. Report co-author Ian White of PTES described the "upturn"  as "welcome good news" which gives grounds for  "cautious optimism".But he added: "We mustn't lose sight of the bigger picture: populations remain almost 60% lower than they were in 2000." The hazel dormouse is famous for spending much of the year asleep. It hibernates from around October to May, spending the winter in a nest on the ground. Even during spring and summer, dormice can go into short periods of deep sleep, known as torpor, when the weather is cold and wet, or food is scarce. This helps the small rodent conserve energy.Researchers believe warmer summers may be reducing the need for torpor, leaving dormice with more energy for feeding and breeding.They say more research is needed to understand what longer-term impacts climate change could have on the species.Dr Charlotte Armitage, an ecologist who worked on the survey, said significant uncertainties remain, including how dormice will respond to warmer, wetter winters.However, she said warmer summer conditions are likely to give the animals more energy to reproduce and raise additional litters."This is good news, but we can't be complacent," she told BBC News."We still need to protect their habitat, do more research into the effects of climate change and carry out effective woodland management for the benefit of dormice."

schema.headline: Dormouse numbers may be helped by warmer summers - survey

title: Brydon Carse given path to England return, Shoaib Bashir dropped and Liam Patterson-White called up
description: England have opened the door for Brydon Carse to return to Test cricket for the tour of South Africa by naming the pace bowler in the Lions squad.Cars
body: England have opened the door for Brydon Carse to return to Test cricket for the tour of South Africa by naming the pace bowler in the Lions squad.Carse could come into the Test squad as cover for Josh Tongue, who will miss the opener to the three-Test series to be at the birth of his second child.England have named a 15-man group for the series, which begins in Johannesburg on 17 December. Uncapped Nottinghamshire left-arm spinner Liam Patterson-White is called up for the first time, at the expense of Shoaib Bashir.Carse has not been part of any England squad since being handcuffed - explained as arrested then de-arrested - outside a nightclub in Derby in August.Although Derbyshire Police have ended their investigation into a potential assault, Carse has been charged by the Cricket Regulator, with a verdict still to come.Carse has continued to play for Durham and has remained available for England selection since the Derby incident.However, England have previously explained his absence by a need for Carse to spend time away from the international arena.Speaking as the Test and Lions squads were announced on Monday, England selector Marcus North said: "The past few months, under investigation, there has been a time where he has stood back, a time of reflection."It's obviously been a challenging time for Brydon, it's one that we haven't felt that the demands of playing international cricket and what he was dealing with wasn't necessarily right for Brydon or for us."There have been numerous conversations over this period. The conclusion is we feel he is in a place where we feel we can introduce him back into the England environment and we feel the Lions is the right place for him to come."England squad for three-Test series in South Africa: Joe Root (captain), Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jacob Bethell, Harry Brook, Sam Cook, Jordan Cox, Ben Duckett, Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence, Liam Patterson-White, Ollie Robinson, Jamie Smith, Josh Tongue.Tongue is missing England's one-day series in Australia with a toe injury and is due to see a specialist in the UK.Depending on the status of his injury, he could play in England's only warm-up game ahead of the South Africa Tests before returning home for the birth, leaving the tourists a seamer light.Carse will be competing with other Lions seamers Henry Crocombe, Olly Stone, Matthew Fisher, Eddie Jack, Matthew Potts and Mitchell Stanley for the chance to cover for Tongue.And North confirmed England will call up "one or two" players to the senior squad."This is where I feel using the Lions tour to our advantage - we have a very strong bowling group in that Lions programme," he said. "That enables us to have a look at where they are at, under competition and training."The tour of South Africa will be England's first under new head coach Stephen Fleming.With the white-ball team currently in Perth preparing for the first one-day against Australia on Friday, Fleming travelled from his home in New Zealand to meet with the rest of the management and select the Test squad.Jacob Bethell returns to the Test team for the first time since July following a knee injury.The left-hander's return creates congestion in the top order after Emilio Gay and Jordan Cox both featured in the 3-0 home win over Pakistan, with North confirming England are yet to settle on their top six for the first Test against South Africa.All-rounder Sam Curran, touted as a potential replacement for former captain Ben Stokes, was not considered because he is getting married. The wedding was planned before Stokes announced his international retirement during the summer.England Lions red-ball squad for two first-class matches in South Africa: Shoaib Bashir, Brydon Carse, James Coles, Mason Crane, Henry Crocombe, Matthew Fisher, Jack Haynes, George Hill, Eddie Jack, Ben Mayes, Ben McKinney, Ollie Pope, Matthew Potts, James Rew, Thomas Rew, Mitch Stanley, Olly Stone, Asa Tribe.England Lions 50-over squad: Rehan Ahmed, Brydon Carse, Mason Crane, Adam Finch, Matthew Fisher, Calvin Harrison, Jack Haynes, George Hill, Ben Mayes, Ben McKinney, Ollie Pope, James Rew, Naavya Sharma, Ekansh Singh, Asa Tribe.Bashir's omission is eye-catching, given the faith England showed in the off-spinner under Stokes and previous Test coach Brendon McCullum.Given a debut at the age of 20 and after playing only six previous first-class matches, Bashir was fast-tracked as England's number-one spinner, becoming the youngest England bowler to 50 Test wickets in the process.However, a broken hand and a lack of form meant he was not picked during last winter's 4-1 defeat in Australia, and conditions meant he bowled in only one of England's six home Tests during the past summer.Bashir was still the only specialist red-ball spinner given a central contract last month, an indication he remained the first choice, though is now effectively dropped from a squad for the first time in his England career. The 23-year-old will instead join Carse in the Lions."Our investment hasn't changed," said North of Bashir. "He is still a very young man, he is someone who we still have a very positive outlook for."We look at each Test series in isolation, and we feel Liam gives us the best balance and that spinner for this tour. We continue to be incredibly invested in Shoaib over the winter."Patterson-White, who turned 28 on Sunday, is called up on the back of strong form for Nottinghamshire and after being given an England development contract.Last season, his 42 wickets were the most by a spinner in Division One of the County Championship, while he can contribute with the bat too, having made three first-class hundreds.Patterson-White may also have benefitted from new coach Fleming's links to Nottinghamshire, the county he once captained."Liam has got some great attributes," said North. "There is a lot of consistency with Liam and his bowling."We feel that has really come and matured during the past two seasons at Nottinghamshire. He has the ability to hold an end, but also get into the game at the back end."We're really excited to see Liam in that Test environment. It's recognition of his development over the past year or so."The Test squad will arrive in South Africa in different groups, with some joining the Lions in late November and others after returning to the UK following their part in the three one-dayers in Australia.From the Test players who are also involved in the T20 series in Australia, white-ball captain Harry Brook, Bethell and Cox will miss the fifth and final match of the series in order to travel to South Africa.For Brook, it will be the first England game he has missed since the T20 tour of Ireland last September. In his absence, all-rounder Will Jacks will captain England for the first time.

schema.headline: Brydon Carse given path to England return, Shoaib Bashir dropped and Liam Patterson-White called up

title: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say
description: A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.The 24-yea
body: A gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and his parents and sister at their home has died in hospital, Polish police say.The 24-year-old was injured after opening fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland, on Saturday, and died early on Monday morning, police said. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said.Officials initially reported the gunman had apparently been inspired by "far-right ideologies", but have since said they are still investigating any possible motivation.After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man. He has not yet been officially named.In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details.However, during a press briefing on Monday morning, Przemysław Nowak, a spokesperson for Poland's National Prosecutor's Office, said investigations into his motive remain ongoing.Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the  attack.Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed.Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister.Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home.Four firearms were found in the gunman's car, including two AR-15 rifles and two handguns, along with several hundred rounds of ammunition, Nowak said. Authorities also seized at least four phones from his car and person, and electronic equipment from his home.Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia.Speaking on Sunday, one of two surgeons who treated victims on the street after the attack said his colleague "undoubtedly" saved the life of a gravely injured police officer.The two surgeons, who were eating near the Main Market Square when the gunman opened fire, rushed to the scene to treat both the attacker and the two injured police officers. Professor Michal Pędziwiatr told the BBC: "We saw the shooting attack. And what a surgeon can do in a situation like this?... We decided to help the victims as soon as possible.""We rushed into the area where the shooting was and started our rescue, because there were no ambulances available, there were no professionals around."Pędziwiatr said his colleague, who has been named by local media as Dr Mateusz Wierdak, used his hand to stem the bleeding from the most severely injured policeman, allowing time for an ambulance to arrive.On Sunday it was reported that both injured officers had emerged from comas.Witnesses who were near the Main Market Square have described their panic and confusion as the attack unfolded. Ruby Catherine Warren, from London, heard gunfire and "yelled at my friends to run and we all sprinted for our lives".She said they "just kept sprinting" until they found a hotel to shelter inside. Tom Brook, from West Yorkshire, was inside a McDonald's near the square when he heard "multiple gunshots and saw people running for cover"."I then walked into the square and saw paramedics working on someone outside [a shop] and there was a dead body covered in foil blankets 20 meters away," he said.

schema.headline: Krakow shooting suspect has died in hospital, police say

title: 'I tossed books across the room': Booker Prize judges reveal 'tussle' over shortlist
description: Past Booker Prize winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the contenders to scoop the prestigious literary award this year, after a shortlis
body: Past Booker Prize winners Marlon James and Douglas Stuart are among the contenders to scoop the prestigious literary award this year, after a shortlist selection process that the judges described as "a tussle".Jamaican writer James is nominated this year for his latest novel The Disappearers; while Scottish author Stuart is shortlisted for John of John.This year's other contenders are award-winning US novelist Elizabeth Strout, and British authors M John Harrison, Luke Kennard and Rebecca Perry.But seven books that appeared on the longlist in July were jettisoned, and Dame Mary Beard, who chaired the judging panel, said agreeing on the final six "has been, to put it mildly, hard work".The winner will receive £50,000 and will be announced in London on Monday evening. The ceremony will be broadcast live on a special edition of BBC Radio 4's Front Row.Scroll down to find out more about this year's nominees.James previously won the Booker Prize in 2015 for A Brief History of Seven Killings, while Stuart won in 2020 for Shuggie Bain.Praising this year's entries when announcing the shortlist in September, Dame Mary added: "English language fiction now is full of talent – talent old and talent new."It's full of wit, seriousness, pleasure, challenge, discomfort and real brilliance, and I think we should be rewarding our novelists a lot more than we do."The other judges included former Booker Prize-shortlisted US novelist Patricia Lockwood, who said she discovered she was "bossier than I believed myself to be" when making the case for or against particular books in the judges' meetings."I was sort of standing up a lot and tossing books across the room and being really active. I was like, 'Wow, yeah, I didn't know I had it in me'."Another judge, poet Raymond Antrobus, told reporters: "All of us individually had a different idea for a shortlist and then it was a tussle."Lockwood jokingly added: "A tussle, yeah. We wrestled like pigs in the mud!"Antrobus said the final choices are connected because they are books that "as well as having heart, also took risk"."These books, we truly believe, cannot be replicated by artificial intelligence. These are very human books for the way they talk about and navigate a lived experience."The judging line-up was completed by journalist, editor and critic Rebecca Liu and Pulp frontman Jarvis Cocker, who said being on the selection panel was "a bit like being in a band".He said: "The way a band makes an appealing noise is by everybody combining, in a way, and if you don't like that then you have to go solo."You get something that you couldn't get [alone] and no-one's in control of it and you make a good noise together. So I hope that's what this shortlist is, a nice noise."Cocker read some of the entries while on tour, and said he joined one judges' meeting online while wearing a dressing gown in a hotel room in Australia at 02:00 local time."When you're on tour, it's quite dull when you're travelling so it was quite good to have something to read," he said."I became known for being in those meetings wearing a towelling robe."The End of Everything by M John HarrisonAn unexplained catastrophe, and the arrival of mysterious alien beings, have turned British society upside down - and a man and his elderly aunt muddle through on the Kent coast. It's the author's first Booker nomination, and he'd be the oldest ever winner at 81.The judges said: "The End of Everything can be read as a thriller, a mystery, a satire, a dystopia, a road novel, a work of realism. The landscape may be bleak, the catastrophe may be immersive, yet there still were moments we found ourselves laughing aloud."The Disappearers by Marlon JamesThis epic, visceral story revolves around a violent attack on eight gay men who had gathered to rehearse a queer play in Kingston, Jamaica, in 1988, and its aftermath. The New York Times called it "a masterpiece, the novel of the decade and possibly of the century thus far".The judges said: "A Jamaican epic from one of the most impactful Caribbean novelists today; readers will love the shifting register of the dialogue and poetic phrasings, often pierced through with sharp, double-edged humour."Black Bag by Luke KennardAn out-of work actor gets a new role - being locked in a black bag during psychology lectures for an entire term as a professor's experiment. The story unfolds into a humorous and poignant satire that makes sharp observations about the state of modern masculinity and creative life.The judges said: "In a wonderfully quirky campus novel, Kennard combines an absurd experiment with a moving story about human frailty, passion, confusion and identity. There's something for everyone here."May We Feed the King by Rebecca PerryA modern-day museum curator is commissioned to recreate a past scene in a historic palace, and becomes immersed in the world of the young, reluctant king whose life she uncovers. It is the debut novel by Perry, who is also a poet and a former competitive trampolinist.The judges said: "An affecting and lush jewel of a novel that moves between our present-day world to a medieval court and unsettles the idea that there's ever one universal historical truth."The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth StroutStrout, a former Pulitzer Prize winner and double Booker nominee, tells the story of a high school history teacher in his 50s who feels adrift in modern America. When a secret emerges, he must face big questions about his relationships and life choices.The judges said: "A novel that engages with the deeply divisive politics of present-day America, without itself becoming divisive. This is the kind of book we need now: a calm antidote to contemporary events."John of John by Douglas StuartThe third novel by Stuart is about a fashion student who is drawn back to his home in a small, religious community in the Outer Hebrides in the mid-1990s. He and his father both nurse secrets. And both are called John.The judges said: "A rich and moving novel about a father and son who live on a remote Scottish island in the 1990s, where small-town secrets and buried shame reverberate to surprising, devastating and even joyous effect."

schema.headline: 'I tossed books across the room': Booker Prize judges reveal 'tussle' over shortlist

title: Jensen Huang: Silicon Valley superstar engulfed by personal scandal
description: Jensen Huang: Why a personal scandal for the face of the AI boom has provoked a national security scareImage source, Getty ImagesByLily JamaliNorth Am
body: Jensen Huang: Why a personal scandal for the face of the AI boom has provoked a national security scareImage source, Getty ImagesByLily JamaliNorth America Technology correspondent and Peter HoskinsBusiness reporterJensen Huang is one of the technology industry's most high-profile figures.He rose to prominence as the business he leads - artificial intelligence (AI) chip giant Nvidia - became one of the world's most valuable companies.As the face of the AI boom, Huang also became close to Donald Trump as the president pushed for the US to keep its dominance of the technology over China.The 63-year-old who was once lauded as the "Taylor Swift of tech" and referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan is now mired in scandal after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang was nine years old when his family moved to the West Coast of the US. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.Huang then worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia.He has an estimated fortune of $155bn, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index."Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine - a biography on Huang, tells the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. Huang has a famously close relationship with Trump. At the recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Elon Musk and Huang.Trump said he had not spoken to the Nvidia boss since news of the investigation emerged."I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what's going on," Trump told reporters, adding that he had "done an amazing job for our country".Image source, Bloomberg via Getty ImagesHuang has long found himself at the centre of US-China tensions. Trump has repeatedly said the two nations are in a race for dominance.Trump has said "whoever wins AI wins", and the fear is that if China gains the upper hand in AI, it will supercharge the country's military and surveillance capabilities.The US advantage is in large part because of US companies like Nvidia, working with producers like the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), which makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips.Since 2022 the US has used various export controls to keep the top tech out of China, which it says helps retain America's competitive edge and protects its national security.But it means companies like Nvidia have been largely locked out of the world's most lucrative market, with Jensen Huang once saying that Nvidia's share of the Chinese market had gone from around 95% to effectively zero. In recent years Huang has engaged in a flurry of shuttle diplomacy, dashing between Washington and Beijing, hoping to find a US-approved way back in, and shaping US policy on China along the way.Sunday's revelations may explain why Huang has failed to bring home the biggest prize of all to Nvidia: the Trump administration's blessing to sell all but its most advanced chips to China.Quarter after quarter of late, Nvidia has been locked out of that lucrative market. Despite his ostensible closeness to Trump, Huang has not managed to wrest this concession from the administration.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Huang is commonly referred to as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan where he was bornHuang founded Nvidia with fellow electrical engineers Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem in 1993.The company was originally known for chips that process graphics, particularly for computer games. Eventually it changed focus to AI, a field it now dominates."In 2012 these machine learning neural net researchers started to use it for that purpose and Jensen immediately recognised that this was going to be a massive industry and the future of computing. He began to pour enormous amounts of resources into building what was essentially the AI hardware market," says Witt. "Today when we think of that, we think of these giant data centres - none of that existed. There were no customers for the stuff he was building. In fact his first customer was Open AI at the time they had 30 people - he actually gave it to them, he donated it to them." Nvidia is now worth some $4.5 trillion, making it one of the most valuable companies ever."The first real neural net of modern times on an Nvidia network was Alex Krizhevsky's Alexnet and they trained that on two Nvidia cards in Alex's bedroom. Now we do the same thing but we do it with 200,000 - 300,000 cards and instead of doing it in a bedroom we do it in a giant barn full of computers called a data centre," adds Witt. "So when you think about a data centre buildout, when you hear the AI infrastructure buildout, Jensen runs a tollbooth. All of that goes through him. And it made his company at least temporarily, the most valuable company in the world."Nvidia's board has announced a probe following reports by the New York Times that Huang had engaged in a romantic relationship with a woman believed by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy.For now, though, Nvidia's board appears to have little appetite for removing Huang, saying in a statement on Sunday that they have "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team".Sources tell the BBC his removal is unlikely because there is so much money at stake. There is also no clear successor to the 63-year old tech boss.Who is Huang's wife?Huang met his wife Lori at Oregon State University, where she was also studying electrical engineering and was his lab partner.They married in 1985, about eight years before he co-founded Nvidia, and have two children, Madison and Spencer.He has credited Lori and Madison for making black leather jackets his signature style.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Lori Huang accompanied her husband at the state dinner held by President Donald Trump for his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in SeptemberIn 2007, the couple founded the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation.  The charitable fund has seen its assets surge in recent years, driven by the soaring value of Nvidia shares, and is estimated to be worth more than $9bn.Its donations include tens of millions of dollars to engineering programmes at Oregon State and Stanford University."Jensen in my conversations with him and in other conversations has gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man. That's very important to him," says Witt. "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways. Both of his children work for Nvidia. Spencer and Maddison. The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."Huang for his part released a statement which said, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."What do we know about the affair?US officials had concluded that Alice Huang had been recruited to spy by China's top intelligence agency, the New York Times reports.She was a top executive at Megaspeed, a data centre company based in Singapore. The firm had been suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China, a concern that Nvidia maintains was investigated and debunked.Surveillance reportedly revealed communications between Alice Huang and an American citizen, who was subsequently identified as Jensen Huang through a process known as "unmasking".It remains unclear what information Alice Huang – who is also known as Huang Le – allegedly passed to Beijing, how valuable it was, or when she is believed to have begun gathering intelligence.Alice Huang did not respond to the paper's request for comment.When the BBC asked Nvidia if the company was aware of intelligence concerns, the company said it was not."We trust that if we were the target of a genuine threat, the US government would have notified us," an Nvidia spokesperson told the BBC.Additional reporting by Ayeshea Perera in Singapore and Helen Davidson in Sydney
